# /dream-on — the Firehorse Dreaming umbrella

You are running the canonical five-step Firehorse Dreaming loop. The user
typed `/dream-on` (or said "dream on") because they want forward motion
without per-step approval. There is exactly **one HIL touch**: plan-mode
approval at step 3.

Input: `$ARGUMENTS` — optional proposal path, topic keyword, or `--next`.

## Execution

### 1. Scan & pick the next artifact

If `$ARGUMENTS` is a path to `.claude/clawdbot/proposals/*.md`, use it directly.
Else:

- Run `node scripts/clawdbot-scan.mjs` to refresh the queue. Surface counts briefly.
- List `.claude/clawdbot/proposals/*.md`. Filter to those whose first 10
  lines do NOT contain `STATUS: PROMOTED` or `STATUS: NO-OP`. Sort by mtime,
  newest first. Pick the top.
- If no unpromoted proposals: pick the top pending queue item from
  `node scripts/clawdbot-scan.mjs --list`.
- If both empty: try `node scripts/clawdbot-scan.mjs --dream-prune` (always
  safe — pure grep, no LLM). If that surfaces a proposal, restart at step 1.
  Otherwise print "Dream queue empty — nothing to do" and stop.

### 2. Build the plan

Read the chosen artifact. Detect kind from filename prefix
(`curate-`, `skill-`, `archival-`, `migration-`) or, for queue items,
from the `## Pending TODOs` section.

Build a numbered TODO list where each line is one concrete edit. Examples:

- `Write .claude/clawdbot/memory/<topic>.md (180 lines)`
- `Edit CLAUDE.md § "Auto-Mode Trust Boundary" (+12 / −3 lines)`
- `git mv skills/risto skills/risto_OLD`
- `node scripts/clawdbot-scan.mjs --done 0e2e931a`
- `node scripts/firehorse-memory-write.mjs --topic <kebab> --title "<title>" --body-file <path>`

### 3. Plan-mode HIL approval (the one HIL touch)

Call `ExitPlanMode` with the numbered TODO list as the plan body. Include:

- A one-sentence summary of what the proposal is.
- The TODO list.
- A footer: "Trust zone: YELLOW. After approval I will execute these
  atomically and stop on any RED-zone touch or runtime ambiguity."

Wait for HIL to exit plan mode. If they reject, respect it; do not retry.
If they edit the plan, use the edited version.

### 4. Execute under /goal

After plan-mode exit, propose a `/goal` directive composed from the plan,
with a mandatory turn-cap clause. Show it for the user to run, e.g.:

> Run `/goal proposal <path> has STATUS: PROMOTED in its first 10 lines AND all approved target paths have been written, or stop after 10 turns` to keep this session driving the work until done.

Slash commands cannot invoke other slash commands, so the user pastes
the suggested `/goal`. Then begin executing the approved TODO list. Each
edit is a normal Edit / Write / Bash call. If a target path already
exists, ask the user `AskUserQuestion(overwrite | append | skip)` —
that is the only allowed mid-execution HIL touch.

For memory-note edits specifically, after writing the local file run:

```
node scripts/firehorse-memory-write.mjs --topic <kebab> --title "<title>" --body-file <path>
```

If `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` are unset, run with `--dry-run`
and note that the CMS dual-write was skipped — the local file is still
authoritative.

### 5. Record (commit + push + **PR**)

After all TODOs are complete:

1. Prepend `> **STATUS: PROMOTED <today>** — see commit for details.`
   to the proposal file. Do NOT delete (CLAUDE.md no-rm rule).
2. For queue items: `node scripts/clawdbot-scan.mjs --done <shortId>`.
3. `git add` the touched paths, commit with a clear message naming the
   proposal that drove the work, `git push -u origin <branch>`.
4. **Open a pull request.** This is mandatory — previous Dreaming
   sessions sometimes pushed without PR-ing, leaving curated work
   stranded on feature branches and invisible to the review queue.
   Use `mcp__github__create_pull_request` with base=`main`,
   head=`<current-branch>`, title summarizing the proposal, body
   listing the touched paths + a "Generated by /dream-on" footer.
   If a PR for this branch already exists, no-op (it'll pick up the
   new commits automatically).
5. Print a one-paragraph summary: paths written, queue ids closed,
   commit SHA, **PR URL**, anything skipped.

## Bail-out rules

- HIL rejects the plan → stop. Do not regenerate a plan unprompted.
- RED-zone file appears in the plan (applying migrations, deploys,
  outbound email, thesis files, Store sync, secrets) → stop and ask.
  Authoring a migration FILE is GREEN; applying it is RED.
- A target path collision the proposal does not address → ask the user
  once via `AskUserQuestion`.
- Auto-mode budget (`CLAUDE_AUTO_MODE_BUDGET`) reached → stop, summarize.

## Examples

```
/dream-on
/dream-on --next
/dream-on .claude/clawdbot/proposals/archival-2026-05-12.md
/dream-on digital-design-gold
```

The third example resumes a specific proposal; the fourth filters to
proposals whose body mentions "digital-design-gold" (case-insensitive).
